definition: Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) is an iterative method for constrained nonlinear optimization, also known as Lagrange-Newton method.
details: SQP methods are used on mathematical problems for which the objective function and the constraints are twice continuously differentiable, but not necessarily convex. SQP methods solve a sequence of optimization subproblems, each of which optimizes a quadratic model of the objective subject to a linearization of the constraints. If the problem is unconstrained, then the method reduces to Newton's method for finding a point where the gradient of the objective vanishes. If the problem has only equality constraints, then the method is equivalent to applying Newton's method to the first-order optimality conditions, or Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, of the problem.

explainer.lead: It is an iterative method for constrained nonlinear optimization, also known as the Lagrange-Newton method. It solves a sequence of quadratic subproblems rather than one hard problem.

tiers.eli5: Like taking a complicated problem and replacing it each round with a simpler stand-in you can actually solve.
tiers.practitioner: Used when objective and constraints are twice continuously differentiable but not necessarily convex; unconstrained it reduces to Newton's method. Pitfall: assumes smoothness, not convexity, so convergence is not guaranteed by convexity.
tiers.paperLevel: Solves a sequence of subproblems, each optimizing a quadratic model of the objective subject to a linearization of the constraints.

explainer.example: Constrained nonlinear optimization where each step optimizes a quadratic model against linearized constraints.
